entries.grounds: PROOF from the code that the dropped ValueError arm never fires given _in_the_way's single caller. (1) `_in_the_way` is called from exactly one site, child_evidence:202, inside `if text is None` (grep '_in_the_way(' over aisef2/validation/tests -> lineage.py:202 only; no test calls it directly). (2) child_evidence sets `text = None` only at lineage.py:188-190 (the `except OSError as e: ... not_there(e)` arm); if `(child / JOURNAL)` held an embedded NUL, `read_text()` would raise ValueError, caught at child_evidence:191-192 (`except ValueError: return UNBEGUN, None`) BEFORE _in_the_way is reached. (3) So when _in_the_way runs, `child / JOURNAL` is NUL-free; every `here` it builds is a prefix of that path (child, then child/'run', child/'run'/'journals', child/'run'/'journals'/'aisef-run.jsonl' — JOURNAL = run/journals/aisef-run.jsonl, a NUL-free constant, lineage.py:115), hence NUL-free. Therefore no ValueError can arise inside the try at lineage.py:215-221, and the removed arm is dead. entries.grounds: `', '.join(...)` becomes `''.join(...)`: the separator between distinct unread run directories is removed. With >=2 unread runs the function concatenates their full paths into one string, e.g. '/tmp/a/run1/tmp/b/run2' instead of '/tmp/a/run1, /tmp/b/run2'. This is reachable: a lineage chain whose runs are one `runs` entry each (lineage.py:708-777), >=2 of them having lost evidence, and `dict.fromkeys` keeps them distinct by path. The result is read by an operator in three refusal messages that tell them which run directory to restore (run.py:530-536 'a faithful copy of the run directory at {unread_runs(inherited)}', verify.py:90-93, bundle_cli.py:962-965); with the separator gone the operator cannot tell the two restore targets apart — a merged, unusable path. This is exactly the contract T09b states ('identifiers stand apart so the operator can lift each of them'). MEASURE: unread_runs[3] vs tests.v2.test_v21_x_lineage_proof = PASS 55/0 (SURVIVED), vacuous (the file never calls unread_runs); x_lineage_gone, which does call it, only tests the single-run case (join of one element — unaffected by the separator), so nothing anywhere exercises >=2 runs. A test is owed.
entries.refutation: INPUT: an account with two distinct unread runs, e.g. account = {'runs': [{'run': '/x/run1', 'unread': ['run1/... is not there']}, {'run': '/y/run2', 'unread': ['run2/... cannot be read']}], 'unread': ['run1/...', 'run2/...'], ...}. READER: lineage.unread_runs (and, end-to-end, the operator refusal message in run.py:536 / verify.py:92 / bundle_cli.py:965 that embeds it). SKETCH: assertEqual(lineage.unread_runs(account), '/x/run1, /y/run2') — or, reader-level, build a lineage whose two ancestor runs both lost their sessions, drive verify()/bundle continue, and assert both run-directory paths appear separated (assertIn('/x/run1', msg) and assertIn('/y/run2', msg) and ', ' between them). Unmutated this passes; the `''.join` mutant yields '/x/run1/y/run2' and fails. (Pairs naturally with the registration gap: register test_v21_x_lineage_gone.py — and the new two-run case — for ::unread_runs so the sole registered file actually calls the function.)

entries.grounds: `getattr(e, 'winerror', None) in _NOT_THERE_WINERROR` becomes `getattr(e, '', None) in _NOT_THERE_WINERROR`. `getattr(e, '', None)` can never find an attribute named '' and always returns None, so the Windows arm degenerates to `None in (21, 123, 1921)` = always False — the winerror classification is disabled. POSIX: equivalent, because `getattr(e, 'winerror', None)` is already None on a POSIX OSError (measured 3.14.7/darwin: both getattr calls return None), so `not_there` reduces to `e.errno in _NOT_THERE` with and without the mutant. WINDOWS: observably different — an OSError whose winerror is 21 (drive not ready), 123 (invalid name) or 1921 (unresolvable reparse point) but whose mapped errno is NOT in _NOT_THERE (e.g. winerror 123 -> errno EINVAL) is classified 'nothing there' by the original and 'a refusal to look' by the mutant. not_there's consumers then diverge on Windows: child_evidence:188-190 (UNBEGUN vs UNREAD), _look:462-466 (swallow-as-absent vs re-raise), _without_a_journal:? (UNBEGUN vs UNREAD). The behaviour is a deliberate, documented contract (lineage.py:449-450 constant + the _NOT_THERE docstring naming the three Windows cases) and the project treats Windows as a real target.
